title: Research Publication: Monitoring Photosynthetic Performance of Papaya Plants Using Multispectral UAV-VTOL Imagery for Precision Agriculture Support

body:
**Yogyakarta, September 1, 2026 –** Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada has once again produced research publication in the field of precision agriculture through a scientific article published in IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science Volume 1667 Year 2026. This research develops an approach to monitor photosynthetic performance of papaya plants using _Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Vertical Take-Off and Landing_ (UAV-VTOL) technology equipped with _multispectral_ sensors to support the implementation of precision agriculture.

Monitoring plant physiological conditions is one of the important aspects in improving the effectiveness of agricultural management. In horticultural plants, particularly papaya, the physiological condition of each plant may differ even though they are located in the same cultivation area. Differences in canopy structure, leaf age, water availability, environmental conditions, and sunlight exposure can affect plant photosynthetic activity.

To date, plant condition observation is generally conducted through direct visual observation. However, this method has limitations because changes in plant physiology cannot always be detected solely from physical appearance. Plants that appear green and healthy do not necessarily have optimal photosynthetic activity. Therefore, monitoring technology is needed that can provide information on plant physiological conditions in a more objective, measurable manner, and covering a wider area.

One important indicator in this research is the _Photosynthetic Electron Transport Rate_ (ETR), which is the rate of electron transport in the photosynthesis process that reflects the activity of photosystem II in plants. ETR information can be used to understand plant photosynthetic performance while identifying the possibility of physiological limitations due to environmental conditions or stomatal regulation.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1199-1-image-37-714x1030.webp)

The research titled "_Multispectral-based Monitoring of Papaya Photosynthetic Performance Using UAV-VTOL for Precision Agriculture Applications_" was conducted by Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, Fahmi Arsyad, Fadel Arya Pradana, Radi, Muneshi Mitsuoka, Lilik Sutiarso, and Takashi Okayasu. This scientific article was published in _IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science_, Volume 1667 (2026), with article number 012003.

The research was conducted on papaya cultivation land (_Carica papaya L._) in Sendangsari, Minggir District, Sleman Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta. This location represents a tropical cultivation environment with diverse canopy characteristics, inter-canopy gaps, and variations in physiological conditions among individual plants.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1199-2-image-38-1030x395.webp)

In its implementation, the research utilized a UAV-VTOL platform equipped with five-channel _multispectral_ imaging sensors, namely _blue_, _green_, _red_, _red-edge_, and _near-infrared_ (NIR). These five channels were used to obtain plant canopy reflectance information related to pigment absorption, chlorophyll content, canopy condition, and vegetation characteristics.

The _multispectral_ image data obtained from the UAV was then combined with direct physiological measurements on each plant. These measurements included ETR, stomatal conductance (gsw), maximum fluorescence (Fm), and other fluorescence parameters. After data filtering, 73 observations of papaya plants were obtained and used as the final dataset in modeling.

In simple terms, this research not only utilized drones to generate plant condition imagery, but also linked spectral information from the air with plant physiological conditions measured directly. Through this approach, _multispectral_ imagery can be utilized to estimate photosynthetic activity at the individual plant level.

##### Collaboration and Support:

This research was conducted through collaboration between Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, and Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Agriculture, Kyushu University, Japan.

This collaboration combines expertise in precision agriculture, remote sensing, UAV technology, plant physiology, _multispectral_ image processing, and data analysis and _machine learning_. This cross-institutional synergy supports the development of plant monitoring methods that integrate direct physiological measurements with air-based remote sensing technology.

The research team expresses appreciation and gratitude to the Working Group Food Security (WGFS 1.2) – Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming, Center for Excellence Among Higher Education Institutions (PUAPT), Universitas Gadjah Mada, for the support of research facilities provided. Appreciation is also extended to Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, for technical support, research collaboration, and scientific assistance throughout the research implementation.

##### Benefits and Impact:

This research contributes to the development of remote sensing-based plant physiological condition monitoring technology to support the implementation of precision agriculture on horticultural commodities, particularly papaya plants. The integration of UAV-VTOL _multispectral_ imagery with physiological measurements and _machine learning_ enables the identification of variations in photosynthetic activity at the individual plant level in a more measurable manner.

Information regarding ETR conditions and photosynthetic productivity grouping can serve as the basis in determining the priority of field scouting, irrigation management evaluation, fertilization assessment, and plant stress risk mapping. Thus, cultivation management can be directed more specifically based on the actual condition of each plant, rather than solely based on visual observation or uniform treatment across the entire cultivation area.

From a technology development perspective, this research also demonstrates the potential of utilizing UAV-VTOL, _multispectral_ sensors, and artificial intelligence in building more informative plant monitoring systems. This approach can help bridge the limitations of manual physiological measurements that require considerable time and effort, especially when applied to larger agricultural areas.

Nevertheless, the model developed in this research is still an initial diagnostic framework that has undergone internal validation. The research dataset is derived from 73 plants at a single location during a single acquisition period, so further testing is required at different locations, seasons, varieties, plant ages, and management conditions before this technology is applied as an operational decision support system.

Looking forward, this approach has the potential to be developed through periodic UAV flights, monitoring of plant physiological changes over time, and integration with data-based agricultural information systems. Such developments are expected to support more accurate, responsive, and efficient cultivation decision-making in the implementation of smart farming.

The complete publication of this research can be accessed through the following DOI: [http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/1667/1/012003](http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/1667/1/012003)

Contact: Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc. Email: ardan.w@ugm.ac.id

##### Linkage with SDGs

-   **SDG 2 – Zero Hunger**, through the development of technology to monitor photosynthetic performance of papaya plants to support productive and sustainable agriculture.
-   **SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure**, through the integration of UAV-VTOL, _multispectral_ sensors, and _machine learning_ in the development of precision agriculture technology.
-   **SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production**, through the provision of plant physiological condition information with the potential to support water and fertilizer management in a more appropriate and efficient manner.
-   **SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals**, through research collaboration between Universitas Gadjah Mada and Kyushu University in developing plant monitoring technology.

original.body:
**Yogyakarta, 1 September 2026 –** Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada kembali menghasilkan publikasi penelitian di bidang pertanian presisi melalui artikel ilmiah yang diterbitkan dalam IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science Volume 1667 Tahun 2026. Penelitian ini mengembangkan pendekatan pemantauan kinerja fotosintesis tanaman pepaya menggunakan teknologi _Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Vertical Take-Off and Landing_ (UAV-VTOL) berbasis sensor _multispectral_ untuk mendukung penerapan pertanian presisi (_precision agriculture_).

Pemantauan kondisi fisiologis tanaman merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam meningkatkan efektivitas pengelolaan pertanian. Pada tanaman hortikultura, khususnya pepaya, kondisi fisiologis setiap tanaman dapat berbeda meskipun berada dalam satu area budidaya yang sama. Perbedaan struktur tajuk, umur daun, ketersediaan air, kondisi lingkungan, hingga paparan sinar matahari dapat memengaruhi aktivitas fotosintesis tanaman.

Selama ini, pengamatan kondisi tanaman umumnya dilakukan melalui pengamatan visual secara langsung. Namun, metode tersebut memiliki keterbatasan karena perubahan fisiologis tanaman tidak selalu dapat diketahui hanya dari penampilan fisiknya. Tanaman yang terlihat hijau dan sehat belum tentu memiliki aktivitas fotosintesis yang optimal. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan teknologi pemantauan yang mampu memberikan informasi kondisi fisiologis tanaman secara lebih objektif, terukur, dan mencakup area yang lebih luas.

Salah satu indikator penting dalam penelitian ini adalah _Photosynthetic Electron Transport Rate_ (ETR), yaitu tingkat laju transport elektron dalam proses fotosintesis yang mencerminkan aktivitas fotosistem II pada tanaman. Informasi ETR dapat digunakan untuk memahami kinerja fotosintesis tanaman sekaligus mengidentifikasi kemungkinan adanya keterbatasan fisiologis akibat kondisi lingkungan maupun regulasi stomata.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1199-1-image-37-714x1030.webp)

Penelitian berjudul “_Multispectral-based Monitoring of Papaya Photosynthetic Performance Using UAV-VTOL for Precision Agriculture Applications_” dilakukan oleh Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, Fahmi Arsyad, Fadel Arya Pradana, Radi, Muneshi Mitsuoka, Lilik Sutiarso, dan Takashi Okayasu. Artikel ilmiah ini diterbitkan dalam _IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science_, Volume 1667 (2026), dengan nomor artikel 012003.

Penelitian dilaksanakan pada lahan budidaya pepaya (_Carica papaya L._) di Sendangsari, Kecamatan Minggir, Kabupaten Sleman, Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta. Lokasi tersebut merepresentasikan lingkungan budidaya tropis dengan karakteristik tajuk tanaman yang beragam, celah antartajuk, serta variasi kondisi fisiologis antar individu tanaman.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1199-2-image-38-1030x395.webp)

Dalam pelaksanaannya, penelitian memanfaatkan platform UAV-VTOL yang dilengkapi sensor pencitraan _multispectral_ lima kanal, yaitu _blue_, _green_, _red_, _red-edge_, dan _near-infrared_ (NIR). Kelima kanal tersebut digunakan untuk memperoleh informasi reflektansi tajuk tanaman yang berkaitan dengan penyerapan pigmen, kandungan klorofil, kondisi tajuk, serta karakteristik vegetasi.

Data citra _multispectral_ yang diperoleh dari UAV kemudian dikombinasikan dengan pengukuran fisiologis secara langsung pada masing-masing tanaman. Pengukuran tersebut mencakup ETR, konduktansi stomata (_stomatal conductance_ atau gsw), fluoresensi maksimum (Fm), serta parameter fluoresensi lainnya. Setelah proses penyaringan data, diperoleh 73 observasi tanaman pepaya yang digunakan sebagai dataset akhir dalam pemodelan.

Secara sederhana, penelitian ini tidak hanya memanfaatkan _drone_ untuk menghasilkan citra kondisi tanaman, tetapi juga menghubungkan informasi spektral dari udara dengan kondisi fisiologis tanaman yang diukur secara langsung. Dengan pendekatan tersebut, citra _multispectral_ dapat dimanfaatkan untuk memperkirakan aktivitas fotosintesis pada tingkat individu tanaman.

##### Kolaborasi dan Dukungan:

Penelitian ini dilaksanakan melalui kolaborasi antara Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada, dengan Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Agriculture, Kyushu University, Jepang.

Kolaborasi tersebut menggabungkan keahlian dalam bidang pertanian presisi, penginderaan jauh, teknologi UAV, fisiologi tanaman, pemrosesan citra _multispectral_, serta analisis data dan _machine learning_. Sinergi lintas institusi ini mendukung pengembangan metode pemantauan tanaman yang mengintegrasikan pengukuran fisiologis secara langsung dengan teknologi penginderaan jauh berbasis udara.

Tim peneliti menyampaikan apresiasi dan terima kasih kepada Working Group Food Security (WGFS 1.2) – Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming, Pusat Unggulan Antar Perguruan Tinggi (PUAPT), Universitas Gadjah Mada, atas dukungan fasilitas penelitian yang diberikan. Apresiasi juga disampaikan kepada Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada, atas dukungan teknis, kolaborasi penelitian, dan bantuan ilmiah selama pelaksanaan penelitian.

##### Manfaat dan Dampak:

Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi terhadap pengembangan teknologi pemantauan kondisi fisiologis tanaman berbasis penginderaan jauh untuk mendukung penerapan pertanian presisi pada komoditas hortikultura, khususnya tanaman pepaya. Integrasi citra _multispectral_ UAV-VTOL dengan pengukuran fisiologis dan _machine learning_ memungkinkan identifikasi variasi aktivitas fotosintesis pada tingkat individu tanaman secara lebih terukur.

Informasi mengenai kondisi ETR dan pengelompokan produktivitas fotosintesis dapat menjadi dasar dalam menentukan prioritas pengamatan lapangan (_field scouting_), evaluasi pengelolaan irigasi, penilaian pemupukan, serta pemetaan risiko stres tanaman. Dengan demikian, pengelolaan budidaya dapat diarahkan secara lebih spesifik berdasarkan kondisi aktual masing-masing tanaman, bukan hanya berdasarkan pengamatan visual atau perlakuan yang seragam pada seluruh area pertanaman.

Dari sisi pengembangan teknologi, penelitian ini juga memperlihatkan potensi pemanfaatan UAV-VTOL, sensor _multispectral_, dan kecerdasan buatan dalam membangun sistem pemantauan tanaman yang lebih informatif. Pendekatan ini dapat membantu menjembatani keterbatasan pengukuran fisiologis secara manual yang membutuhkan banyak waktu dan tenaga, terutama ketika diterapkan pada area pertanian yang lebih luas.

Meskipun demikian, model yang dikembangkan dalam penelitian ini masih merupakan kerangka diagnostik awal yang telah melalui validasi internal. Dataset penelitian berasal dari 73 tanaman pada satu lokasi dan satu periode akuisisi, sehingga diperlukan pengujian lebih lanjut pada lokasi, musim, varietas, umur tanaman, dan kondisi pengelolaan yang berbeda sebelum teknologi ini diterapkan sebagai sistem pendukung keputusan operasional.

Ke depan, pendekatan ini berpotensi dikembangkan melalui penerbangan UAV secara berkala, pemantauan perubahan fisiologis tanaman dari waktu ke waktu, serta integrasi dengan sistem informasi pertanian berbasis data. Pengembangan tersebut diharapkan dapat mendukung pengambilan keputusan budidaya yang lebih akurat, responsif, dan efisien dalam penerapan _smart farming_.

Publikasi lengkap penelitian ini dapat diakses melalui DOI berikut: [http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/1667/1/012003](http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/1667/1/012003)

Kontak: Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc. Email: ardan.w@ugm.ac.id

##### Keterkaitan dengan SDGs

-   **SDG 2 – Tanpa Kelaparan**, melalui pengembangan teknologi pemantauan kinerja fotosintesis tanaman pepaya untuk mendukung pertanian yang produktif dan berkelanjutan.
-   **SDG 9 – Industri, Inovasi, dan Infrastruktur**, melalui integrasi UAV-VTOL, sensor multispektral, dan _machine learning_ dalam pengembangan teknologi pertanian presisi.
-   **SDG 12 – Konsumsi dan Produksi yang Bertanggung Jawab**, melalui penyediaan informasi kondisi fisiologis tanaman yang berpotensi mendukung pengelolaan air dan pupuk secara lebih tepat dan efisien.
-   **SDG 17 – Kemitraan untuk Mencapai Tujuan**, melalui kolaborasi penelitian antara Universitas Gadjah Mada dan Kyushu University dalam pengembangan teknologi pemantauan tanaman.
